title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Animal and Range Science (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Animal and Range Science (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which one is odd about feed digestive anatomy in farm animals?
questions.explanation: Sensory organ is not directly involved in the digestion of feed. Accessory organs, gastro-intestinal tract, and organs directly digesting feed are all part of the digestive system in farm animals.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a sign of oestrus in ewes and/or does?
options: Lack of interest in feed intake
questions.explanation: All listed options are signs of oestrus in ewes and/or does.

questions.questionText: In the digestive system of the larval stage of silkworm, in which part does digestion and assimilation of food take place?
questions.explanation: Digestion and assimilation of food in the larval stage of silkworm primarily occurs in the mid-gut, which is specialized for these functions. The fore-gut mainly serves for food intake and the hind-gut for waste elimination.

questions.questionText: One of the following is true about legumes:
options: Legumes tend to shatter badly than grasses
Stem of legumes contains higher percentages of protein than its leaves
questions.explanation: All statements about legumes are true.

questions.questionText: One is not considered in feed cost estimation:
questions.explanation: Feeding is not typically included in feed cost estimation.

questions.questionText: Which anatomical adaptation of camels enables walking over soft sand without sinking?
questions.explanation: Pad-like feet help camels walk over soft sand without sinking.

questions.questionText: Select from the list below non-conventional feeds type of our country:
options: By-product from the wheat milling industry
questions.explanation: Cafeteria leftover and vegetable waste are considered non-conventional feeds.

questions.questionText: Which one is/are major constraints of dairy development system in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: All listed options are major constraints of dairy development in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: From the following dairy production systems, which one is a major source of milk?
questions.explanation: Highland Smallholder is a major source of milk in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives, one is true about mulberry silk.
options: Mulberry silk is superior to other silk types
It is produced by other than mulberry silkworm
It is produced from Eri silk worm
It is harvested from the forest from any types of silkworm
questions.explanation: Mulberry silk is considered superior to other silk types.

questions.questionText: What is a recommended method for seeding pasture crops to ensure good soil contact with seed especially around mountains?
options: Sprinkling seeds on the soil surface
questions.explanation: Drilling seeds into the soil ensures good soil contact.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about risks of cloning?
questions.explanation: While cloning has risks, 'die mysteriously' is not a recognized risk.

questions.questionText: The generic name of which of these is Apis?
questions.explanation: Apis is the generic name for honey bees.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about DNA?
options: Each DNA molecule is a single gene
DNA molecules are in the shape of double-strand helix
mRNA molecules are in the shape of double-strand helix
questions.explanation: DNA molecules are indeed in the shape of a double-strand helix.

questions.questionText: _________ is detected by monitoring and usually expressed as improving, declining or stable.
questions.explanation: Rangeland trend is monitored and expressed as improving, declining, or stable.

questions.questionText: __________ is the difference between the mean of selected parents and the population mean before selection.
questions.explanation: Selection differential is the difference between the mean of selected parents and the population mean.

questions.questionText: Which one is a sex-limited trait?
questions.explanation: Mammary gland development is a sex-limited trait.

questions.questionText: Which of the following type of poultry houses has the most space and freedom?
questions.explanation: Free range poultry houses provide the most space and freedom.

questions.questionText: Beef cattle animals with a common origin, selection history and having physical characteristics that distinguish them from others are called:
questions.explanation: A breed is defined by common origin and distinguishing characteristics.

questions.questionText: Which sheep breeds in Ethiopia are producing the most prominent coarse wool?
questions.explanation: Menz sheep breed is known for producing prominent coarse wool.

questions.questionText: Compared with other indigenous sheep breeds of Ethiopia, which one is more prolific?
questions.explanation: Horro sheep are known for their high prolificacy among indigenous Ethiopian sheep breeds, with higher twinning rates than other breeds like Black-head Somali.

questions.questionText: A phenomenon when the performance of individuals/progeny is higher than the average of the two parents is called:
questions.explanation: Heterosis or hybrid vigor refers to the phenomenon of offspring performing better than their parents.

questions.questionText: Which one are advantages of keeping indigenous breeds?
options: Produce and reproduce on poor quality feed
questions.explanation: All listed options are advantages of indigenous breeds.

questions.questionText: __________ is a process in which a bright light is shone through an egg to enable identifying defects or fertile and infertile eggs.
questions.explanation: Candling is the process used to identify defects in eggs.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the gizzard in a chicken?
questions.explanation: The gizzard's purpose is to grind food.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the period of sexual receptivity commonly referred to as 'heat'?
questions.explanation: Estrus is the period of sexual receptivity.

questions.questionText: From the following statements, one is false about the components of sericulture?
options: Cultivation of food for silk moth
It is the processing center of synthetic fiber
Harvesting and reeling of raw silk
questions.explanation: The processing center of synthetic fiber is not a component of sericulture.

questions.questionText: Exotic breed sheep adapted and crossed with indigenous sheep breeds for meat production in Ethiopia:
questions.explanation: Dorper sheep are known for meat production and are crossed with indigenous breeds.

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic feature of legume species that distinguishes them from grasses?
questions.explanation: Legumes are distinguished by their ability to fix nitrogen.

questions.questionText: In the classification of domestic fowls, which term refers to a subdivision within a breed based on specific characteristics such as color or feather patterns?
questions.explanation: Variety refers to a subdivision within a breed based on specific characteristics.

questions.questionText: One of the following is different in the life cycle of silkworm from the other stages?
questions.explanation: Pupa is a distinct stage in the life cycle of a silkworm.

questions.questionText: The following are the advantages of oestrus synchronization except:
options: Reducing or eliminating the labor of detecting oestrus
Allowing the producer to schedule the breeding and calving
Enabling more animals to be artificially inseminated
Increasing the length of the breeding season
questions.explanation: Oestrus synchronization does not increase the length of the breeding season.

questions.questionText: From the following protein types, one is the component of silk?
questions.explanation: Fibroin is the primary protein component of silk.

questions.questionText: Which of the following rangeland types receives low annual precipitation?
questions.explanation: Desert grasslands receive low annual precipitation.

questions.questionText: When we compared dromedary and Bactrian camels, Bactrian camels have:
questions.explanation: Bactrian camels have one more hump than dromedary camels.

questions.questionText: Which one is the following clinical method of pregnancy diagnosis?
questions.explanation: All listed methods can be used for pregnancy diagnosis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a common method used to control weed infestation in pastures, thus contributing to pasture improvement?
questions.explanation: Applying selective herbicides is a common method for controlling weeds.

questions.questionText: Which term refers to a mature female bird that is actively laying eggs?
questions.explanation: A hen is a mature female bird that is actively laying eggs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key characteristic of rangeland ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Limited precipitation is a key characteristic of rangeland ecosystems.

questions.questionText: Feed formulation method used if feed ingredients are more than three:
questions.explanation: Algebraic methods are used for formulating feeds with more than three ingredients.

questions.questionText: Amongst honey bees, the workers are:
questions.explanation: Worker bees are female.

questions.questionText: ------------- is described as a situation where one gene affects multiple traits.
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy refers to one gene affecting multiple traits.

questions.questionText: Which of the following agronomic practices is essential for successful establishment of pasture crops?
questions.explanation: Timely seedbed preparation is essential for establishing pasture crops.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of over seeding in pasture improvement strategies?
questions.explanation: Over seeding aims to improve forage quality and quantity.

questions.questionText: Characteristics of crop residues except:
questions.explanation: Crop residues typically have low nutritive value.

questions.questionText: A relationship between lion and grass indicates:
questions.explanation: The relationship between lion and grass is neutralism.

questions.questionText: Concepts representing nearly the same character:
options: Inorganic constituent ---------> made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen
Organic constituent ---------> made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen
questions.explanation: The option 'Organic constituent ---------> commonly plant origin' represents the correct relationship. Organic constituents in feeds are indeed commonly of plant origin.

questions.questionText: _______ is the differences between individuals of the same species or breed for the same trait or character.
questions.explanation: Variation refers to differences between individuals of the same species.

questions.questionText: A type of beef cattle production system in arid and semi-arid areas where range is the main feed resource is:
questions.explanation: Pastoralism is the production system in arid and semi-arid areas.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about protein classification based on structure?
questions.explanation: Fibrous proteins are a classification based on structure.

questions.questionText: Is the procedure of identifying and documenting diversity within and between distinct breeds, based on their observable attributes?
questions.explanation: Phenotypic characterization involves identifying observable attributes.

questions.questionText: Rutting is:
options: Period of strong sexual desire in female camel
Is a time when male reaches maturity
Period of strong sexual desire in male camel
Is a time when female reaches maturity
questions.explanation: Rutting refers to the period of strong sexual desire in male camels.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is always true about feed intake and digestibility?
options: As feed intake increases, digestibility always increases
As digestibility increases, intake will increase
As digestibility increases, intake increases to a certain level
They do not have any relationship
questions.explanation: As digestibility increases, intake increases to a certain level.

questions.questionText: The major difference between proximate and Van Soest feed chemical composition analysis is/are:
questions.explanation: The major difference lies in carbohydrate estimation.

questions.questionText: What will happen if a male dromedary and female Bactrian camels mate each other?
options: Male camel may injure the female second hump
The male's legs are too short to reach the female genitalia
Male camel may lose his balance and may injure himself
questions.explanation: Infertility occurs when dromedary and Bactrian camels mate.

questions.questionText: _______ is defined as the mothers and fathers of the future bulls?
questions.explanation: Nucleus refers to the breeding stock for future bulls.

questions.questionText: How does the body size of the hen and weather conditions affect the number of eggs that can be set for natural incubation?
options: Larger body size and warm weather allow for setting more eggs
Smaller body size and cold weather allow for setting more eggs
Larger body size and cold weather allow for setting more eggs
Smaller body size and warm weather allow for setting more eggs
questions.explanation: Larger body size and warm weather allow for setting more eggs.

questions.questionText: Air dry basis of feed dry matter is when feeds:
options: Equilibrate to about 90% after a prolonged aerobic storage
Equilibrate to fresh harvest from plot
Equilibrate to total moisture removal from the sample
Comparable to the nutrient content of the feed
questions.explanation: Air dry basis refers to when feeds equilibrate to about 90% dry matter (or 10% moisture) after prolonged aerobic storage at ambient temperature. Total moisture removal would be oven-drying, not air-drying.

questions.questionText: --------------- is a condition or situation when a recessive allele does not affect the phenotype of the heterozygous?
questions.explanation: Complete dominance is when a recessive allele does not affect the phenotype.

questions.questionText: Among the following, one is not correct about dressing percentage:
options: Dressing percentage varies with animal species
Internal fat deposits, kidney fat and channel fat have an effect on carcass percentage
Gut fill has an influence on dressing percentage
As fasting period to slaughter weight increases, dressing percentage will decrease
questions.explanation: As fasting period increases, dressing percentage typically increases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the function of hydrochloric acid?
options: Catalyzes the conversion of the innocent pre-enzyme pepsinogen to pepsin
Kills bacteria and other harmful micro-organisms
questions.explanation: All of the options (activating proteolysis enzymes, catalyzing the conversion of pepsinogen to pepsin, and killing harmful microorganisms) are functions of hydrochloric acid in the digestive system.

questions.questionText: From the following characteristics, one is true about Apis mellifera Scutellata:
options: Small in size & yellow in color
Adapted to short raining & fast flowering condition
Have relatively high tendency of migratory & reproductive swarming
questions.explanation: Apis mellifera Scutellata has a high tendency for migratory and reproductive swarming.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a beef carcass component?
questions.explanation: Stomach components are not considered part of the beef carcass.

questions.questionText: The quality of a feedstuff depends on the following except:
questions.explanation: Animal type does not directly affect the quality of a feedstuff.

questions.questionText: An accelerated growth when feed becomes abundant during the wet season is:
questions.explanation: Compensatory growth occurs when feed becomes abundant.

questions.questionText: What is the chromosome number of sheep?
questions.explanation: The chromosome number of domestic sheep (Ovis aries) is 54, consisting of 27 pairs of chromosomes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not under the categories of ration type?
questions.explanation: Costly is not a recognized category of ration type.

questions.questionText: When is the best time to do queen rearing?
options: When there are enough drones available
questions.explanation: The best time for queen rearing is when there are enough drones available.

questions.questionText: Systematic measurement of performance in a population is:
questions.explanation: Performance testing involves systematic measurement of performance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about DNA?
options: At the beginning of protein synthesis, a section of a DNA molecule unwinds and unzips
All of our DNA is normally located in the nucleus of our cells
DNA is composed of amino acid, nitrogen base, sugar and phosphate
questions.explanation: DNA unwinds and unzips at the beginning of protein synthesis.

questions.questionText: One is not a characteristic of arid and semi-arid areas where camels are extremely well adapted:
options: High radiant energy falling on the ground
questions.explanation: Sufficient rainfall is not characteristic of arid and semi-arid areas.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a useful product of Apiculture?
questions.explanation: Regular jelly is not a product of apiculture. The useful products from beekeeping include honey, beeswax, bee venom, propolis, and royal jelly (which is different from regular jelly).

questions.questionText: The distinguishable feature of vitamins is/are:
options: Most feeds consist of sufficient amounts of most vitamins
Need no digestion in the body
questions.explanation: Vitamins need no digestion in the body.

questions.questionText: From the following, which one is not true?
options: Indigenous cattle are slow to reach sexual maturity than exotic breeds
Indigenous cattle have long calving intervals than exotic breeds
Indigenous cattle have high fat content than exotic breeds
questions.explanation: None of the statements are false - they are all true. Indigenous cattle typically mature slower, have longer calving intervals, and have higher milk fat content compared to exotic breeds.

questions.questionText: _______ is beekeeping equipment which is used for reducing the tendency of bees to sting and direct bees away from areas of the hive being worked.
questions.explanation: A smoker is used to calm bees and direct them away from the area being worked.

questions.questionText: Polysaccharides carbohydrate is/are:
options: Any class of animal can digest
questions.explanation: Polysaccharides can be hydrolyzed by acid and alkali.

questions.questionText: How does an imbalanced feed affect egg production in hens?
options: Has no effect on egg production
questions.explanation: Imbalanced feed typically decreases egg production in hens.

questions.questionText: How long does it take for a fertilized chicken egg to hatch once it has been laid?
questions.explanation: It takes approximately 21 days for a fertilized chicken egg to hatch.

questions.questionText: The following is/are means of fertility performance expression in sheep and goat:
questions.explanation: All listed options are means of expressing fertility performance.

questions.questionText: Which one is the site of milk synthesis in the udder?
questions.explanation: Milk synthesis occurs in the epithelial cells of the udder.

questions.questionText: Based on the chemical nature, one of the following is not polymer in nature:
questions.explanation: Lipids are not polymers; they are made up of fatty acids.

questions.questionText: What is the definition of hatchability in poultry reproduction?
options: The number of eggs laid by a bird
The proportion of incubated eggs that hatch
The time it takes for eggs to hatch
The weight of the hatched chicks
questions.explanation: Hatchability refers to the proportion of incubated eggs that successfully hatch.

questions.questionText: During animal feeding, it is advisable to mix:
options: 85-90% of plant proteins with 10-15% animal proteins
70% plant proteins with 30% oil seed cake proteins
questions.explanation: Mixing 85-90% plant proteins with 10-15% animal proteins is advisable.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a temperate dairy breed?
questions.explanation: Barca type is not recognized as a temperate dairy breed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of local chickens?
questions.explanation: Local chickens are known for their resistance to diseases.

questions.questionText: One is the source of genetic variation in farm animals:
questions.explanation: All listed options are sources of genetic variation.

questions.questionText: Which one is the best method of semen collection for all animals?
questions.explanation: Artificial vagina is considered the best method for semen collection.

questions.questionText: Which one is not production record type information in beef cattle production?
questions.explanation: Milk yield is not typically recorded in beef cattle production.

questions.questionText: The primary objectives of a rangeland inventory are:
questions.explanation: The primary objective is to assess vegetation attributes.

questions.questionText: At which stage of the estrus cycle does follicle rupture and release of the egg occur?
questions.explanation: Follicle rupture and egg release occur during estrus.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following plant characteristics reflects an upward trend?
options: Decline in vegetation composition or density
Better forage plants unavailable to livestock
questions.explanation: Desirable plants being vigorous reflects an upward trend.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the feature of the highland sheep-barley production system:
options: Rangeland is the main land resource
Feed resources are usually household wastes
Temperature is the main factor determining productivity
questions.explanation: The altitude of the highland sheep-barley production system is typically between 1500 - 2000 m.a.s.l.

questions.questionText: One of the following is true about Ribosome:
options: Site of oxygen consumption within the cell
questions.explanation: Ribosomes have two subunits and are involved in protein synthesis.

questions.questionText: In Ethiopian rangelands, they are divided based on the following, except:
questions.explanation: Moisture indices are not typically used to classify Ethiopian rangelands.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the total genetic variation to the total phenotypic or observed variation is termed as:
questions.explanation: Heritability in a broad sense refers to this ratio.

questions.questionText: ________ is/are needs, views, decisions, and active participation of farmers from inception through to implementation during breed improvements?
questions.explanation: Community-based breeding programs involve active participation of farmers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a major source of feed around highland?
questions.explanation: Natural pasture is a major source of feed in highland areas.

questions.questionText: Which volatile fatty acids primarily control the amount of milk produced from cows?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid primarily controls milk production in cows.

questions.questionText: The following are benefits of MOET except:
options: Increasing the number of offspring produced by valuable females
Decreasing the population base of rare or endangered breeds or species
Ex situ preservation of endangered populations
Increasing rates of genetic improvement in breeding programs
questions.explanation: Decreasing the population base of rare breeds is not a benefit of MOET.

questions.questionText: Among the following, one indicates ration cost:
questions.explanation: Cheap ration directly indicates the cost aspect of a feed ration. Balanced ration refers to nutritional adequacy, not specifically to cost.
